_note: What the user asked and corrected while this project was built, each turned into a general lesson the architect applies to every project (wenart/blender/architect_lessons.py; user request of 25 Oct 2026: 'the architect should ask the questions and corrections I was asking all along the build; use AI to understand what I was asking and keep developing with the future requests'). checks: the architect rules that check it on every build (architect.ORDER ids) or 'build' (the build does it by itself); status: rule (a rule checks it), built (code does it), open (no automatic check yet: the AI architect looks for it on every run and it is the next rule to write), process (how we work). Add a new request with: python -m wenart.agent.lessons add "<the request>"

lessons.request: real04 outside renders are not that good, first start giving some material to the outside walls, they seem blank concrete
lessons.lesson: Every outer wall carries a facade finish (render, stone, cladding) with a plinth, slab bands, copings and window surrounds; never bare concrete.
lessons.question: Does every outer wall carry a facade finish, with a plinth, bands and copings?

lessons.request: there is a bulge in bodrum kat looks like a balcony there should not be there; bulge at the side of the pool
lessons.lesson: Nothing sticks out of the facade unless drawn: a basement window gets a light well or a court only when the ground outside is above its sill, never on a terrace that lies below it.
lessons.question: Does anything stick out of the facade that the drawing does not show?

lessons.request: start using outside doors; there are new windows you can try to use
lessons.lesson: Outer doors and windows are real products from the library with see-through glass; a door to a terrace is mostly glass, in the windows' frame finish.
lessons.question: Is every outer door and window a real product with glass, and every terrace door glazed?

lessons.request: start using the new library items for the outside items, plants cars etc
lessons.lesson: The site is furnished like a real garden: trees, shrubs, hedges, lawn, cars on the parking, from the library.
lessons.question: Is the garden furnished: plants, trees, hedges, cars where they belong?

lessons.request: rain gutters you can include; rain gutters going on the air, they need to be connected to walls instead of flying
lessons.lesson: Gutters run along every eave and downpipes run down solid walls to the ground; nothing hangs in the air.
lessons.question: Do the gutters and downpipes hang on the building and reach the ground?

lessons.request: roof not looking good may require a rework; roof still not looking realistic enough, there seem to be some gaps
lessons.lesson: The roof is closed and real: no gaps, eaves with a fascia, ridges and hips, its form following the plan.
lessons.question: Is the roof closed, with real eaves, fascia, ridges and hips?

lessons.request: it seems there is no access to the pool, how will people walk to the pool?
lessons.lesson: Every terrace and pool deck can be reached: from a door at its level or by steps and a path from the site's paths.
lessons.question: Can people reach every terrace and pool deck?

lessons.request: design a module called architect that can ask these kind of questions and make necessary changes; make the architect more clever asking better and better questions; don't restrict this to only 16 questions
lessons.lesson: The architect asks every rule of every element (thousands of questions), fixes what code can fix safely, asks the user the rest with options, and the AI on the pod answers the open ones.
lessons.question: Has every element been asked every rule that applies to it?

lessons.request: make the top down view a bit angled; give a better angle from right up to left down and halve the walls preventing the views
lessons.lesson: The top-down views look from the north-east at about 35 degrees with the walls cut at 0.6 m and the windows marked.
lessons.question: Do the top-down views show every room clearly?

lessons.request: try to have an access from the outside instead of including the door
lessons.lesson: Reach a terrace from outside (steps and a path) before turning a drawn window into a door: drawn openings stay as drawn (26 Oct 2026: except a window between two rooms where one has no door at all: that is its misread door, architect W2).
lessons.question: Is a terrace reached from outside before any drawn window becomes a door?

lessons.request: no inside window should be outside
lessons.lesson: A window between two rooms is a reading error: it moves to the dark room's outer wall.
lessons.question: Does every window look outside?

lessons.request: yes (enlarge the play room windows)
lessons.lesson: A habitable room gets glass of at least a tenth of its floor; too little glass: the windows are enlarged.
lessons.question: Does every habitable room get enough daylight?

lessons.request: yes (the two kitchens are separate on purpose)
lessons.lesson: A separate kitchen may be meant: the architect asks before joining rooms and keeps the answer.
lessons.question: Is a separate kitchen meant?

lessons.request: it's unacceptable to see the clashing furniture at this stage
lessons.lesson: No two pieces of furniture cut each other in any render; clashes are planned apart before the build.
lessons.question: Does any piece cut another?

lessons.request: this section is not making any sense at all, rework it, make it make sense (the east pool deck beside the basement)
lessons.lesson: A terrace beside the house sits at the floor its doors and windows serve, never half way between floors; no pit is cut into a terrace; mirrored twins match; walls over 1.2 m step back as planted terraces or carry a guard.
lessons.question: Does every terrace sit at a floor level that makes sense with the house and its twin?

lessons.request: there is no taste in the furniture selection; make something to develop a tasteful selection of furniture
lessons.lesson: The furniture of a room and of the house is one coherent set: one design language, one or two wood tones, one metal finish, a colour palette from the style (60-30-10), real proportions, and one statement piece per room.
lessons.question: Does the furniture of every room look chosen together, in the style?

lessons.request: there is not enough decor around
lessons.lesson: Rooms are styled like a magazine shoot: every table, console, shelf and nightstand carries a small group of decor, walls carry art, every living room and bedroom has plants, lamps, a rug, cushions and a throw.
lessons.question: Is every room styled with enough decor?

lessons.request: furniture groups are not sufficient
lessons.lesson: Every room is complete for its use: a sofa with a coffee table, side tables, a floor lamp and a rug; a bed with two nightstands and lamps (and a bench in a large room); a dining table with its chairs, a pendant and a sideboard.
lessons.question: Is every furniture group complete?

lessons.request: there are pillows on top of the beds and sofas that seem to be floating
lessons.lesson: Cushions and pillows rest on and lean against their seat or headboard and sink a little into it; no cushion on a model that has its own.
lessons.question: Does every cushion rest on its seat or bed?

lessons.request: is that table on the terrace ok? is that a table suitable for the terrace? is the door to the terrace ok?
lessons.lesson: A terrace is furnished with outdoor pieces (metal, teak, rattan, stone; no indoor desks or upholstery) and reached through a glazed door.
lessons.question: Is the furniture on every terrace made for outside, and its door glazed?

lessons.request: better architectural details needed, better internal stairs, better finishes in the fences on top of the parapets
lessons.lesson: Details are built like real products: stairs with comfortable risers, tread plates with nosings, a balustrade and a handrail; guards of 1 m with gaps under 0.11 m; a coping on every parapet; one balustrade language for the house.
lessons.question: Are the stairs, guards and parapets detailed like real products?

lessons.request: fixes need to be general: they need to work for every project I can throw at this, old and new
lessons.lesson: Every fix is a general rule with a test, never a patch for one project.

lessons.request: every project can use any library item; do not restrict with commercial only, the important thing is to look good and fit together with a style
lessons.lesson: Library models are chosen for the look of the render (fitting together, carrying the style), not for their licence (licence_mode relaxed).

lessons.request: increase the drawing reading functions so the pod can take care of problems like this
lessons.lesson: A reading problem is fixed in the reader, so the pod handles the next drawing of that kind alone.

lessons.request: the architect should ask the questions and corrections I was asking all along; use AI to understand them and keep developing with future requests
lessons.lesson: Every new request or correction of the user becomes a lesson here (python -m wenart.agent.lessons add); open lessons are checked by the AI architect on every run until a rule checks them.

lessons.request: From now on every run is against its latest run compare not according to milestones
lessons.lesson: Every before / after compares the new run with the project's latest run before it (never a milestone run); the new run then becomes the latest.

lessons.request: fix should be general, it is not a fix for real06 it must be a fix for the project don't ever forget that
lessons.lesson: Every fix is a general rule of the pipeline for every project; the project that showed the problem is only the test case.

lessons.request: why there is that many rain gutters in real06
lessons.lesson: Gutters run straight along each facade under the eaves (facade jogs shallower than 0.6 m are closed under the roof); downpipes stand only at the building's corners, at least 3 m apart, about one per 50 m2 of roof.
lessons.question: Do the gutters run straight and do the downpipes stand only at the corners, 3 m apart or more?

lessons.request: why the sink is so low
lessons.lesson: Every fixture works at its working height: a washbasin's rim at 0.80-0.90 m (a wall-hung model hangs there; a bowl too shallow to hang needs a counter and is not taken alone).
lessons.question: Is every washbasin, sink and worktop at its working height?

lessons.request: why doors are up
lessons.lesson: Every door stands on the floor of the rooms it joins; the plans' level marks are read in the section's height frame (the ground floor's printed mark is building z 0).
lessons.question: Does every door stand on its floor?

lessons.request: real06 windows second floor what is that? are the people going to jump of from it? terrible
lessons.lesson: No opening on an upper floor reaches the floor without a real guard: a door or bare gap with nothing outside is a window at the floor's sill; a French window gets a full-width glass guard 1.10 m high; every stair void edge gets a balustrade.
lessons.question: Could anybody fall out of an upper-floor opening or into a stair void?

lessons.request: still with the furniture replacement it is not seen like a stylish house; the house needs to make sense and needs to look very stylish
lessons.lesson: The house reads as one design: one door and window language in the house's style (clear glass, no panelled doors in a modern house), one model per role in a group, one dining set per room, no folding or garden chairs indoors, no piece with its back to the room.
lessons.question: Do the furniture, doors and windows look like one designed set in the house's style?

lessons.request: I want AI to figure out all of these kind of things before I look at it; I need ai models to see understand and fix everything before even I look at it
lessons.lesson: The architect settles every open point that has a safe fix by itself (its default); the AI architect answers the rest; the AI inspector asks a visitor's questions (Q1-Q8) of every render, sends each finding to its fix and reports what is left before the user looks.

lessons.request: AI inspector: vision model reviews every final render ... reviewing the 3d model itself could be better solution rather than individual renders investigate decide apply
lessons.lesson: Review the 3D model itself first: every element of the model as built is measured (doors on their floors, working heights, guards, doors into the air, rain water, one opening language, rooms that make sense), on every floor, before any render; the vision model looks at the model's floors from above (every room) and the renders only for the look.
lessons.question: Was every element of the built model checked, not only what the cameras frame?
